function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""Core TLS path for the data-sync client.

Pulls the current dataset from the internal sync endpoint over HTTPS and writes it
out. The client builds its TLS verification context from the certifi CA bundle:
``certifi.where()`` supplies the trusted public-web root certificates, and the
corporate internal CA is layered on top so the internally-issued sync endpoint also
verifies. Certificate verification stays on for every request — the set of public
roots the client trusts is exactly the set the installed certifi bundle ships.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import ssl
import tomllib
import urllib.request

import certifi

CONFIG_PATH = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "config" / "sync.toml"


def load_config(path: pathlib.Path = CONFIG_PATH) -> dict:
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return tomllib.load(fh)


def build_context(cfg: dict) -> ssl.SSLContext:
    """Build the TLS verification context.

    Public-web trust roots come from the certifi bundle (``certifi.where()``); the
    corporate internal CA is layered on for endpoints issued under it. Verification
    stays enabled (``CERT_REQUIRED`` + hostname checking).
    """
    tls = cfg["tls"]
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
    ctx.load_verify_locations(cafile=tls["internal_ca"])
    return ctx


def fetch_dataset(cfg: dict, ctx: ssl.SSLContext) -> bytes:
    src = cfg["source"]
    url = f"{src['base_url']}/{src['dataset']}"
    opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPSHandler(context=ctx))
    with opener.open(url, timeout=cfg["network"]["timeout_seconds"]) as resp:
        return resp.read()


def sync(cfg: dict, dest: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    """Fetch the dataset over verified TLS and write it out; return a small summary."""
    ctx = build_context(cfg)
    data = fetch_dataset(cfg, ctx)
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest.write_bytes(data)
    return {"bytes": len(data), "dest": str(dest)}

# Approved sync environment
Use .venv/bin/pip install --no-index --find-links /opt/artifacts certifi==2023.7.22. The client uses this public-root bundle plus /etc/ssl/internal/corp-root-ca.pem for the container-local service; verification stays enabled. Run bin/sync.sh and deliver logs/dataset.csv.
